strengths: Comments in [tool.ruff] and [tool.ruff.lint] match the settings: select equals the ruff defaults (E4, E7, E9, F) plus UP, and the four ignored UP rules match the stated typing-module spelling convention.
requires-python >=3.11 agrees with ruff target-version py311, and the 3.14 runtime pin lives in .python-version as the comment says.
[tool.uv] package = false fits a script-style repo that imports conversion.* from the repo root, and uv.lock is tracked for reproducible installs.
Dev tools (pytest, ruff) sit in a [dependency-groups] dev group, not in runtime dependencies.
Native dependencies (pydantic-core, rpds-py) lock wheels for cp311 through cp314, so both the requires-python >=3.11 floor and the 3.14 pin in .python-version install without a source build.
Pipfile runtime dependencies carry over exactly, pydantic>=2 floor included, and the lock's package.metadata matches pyproject.toml, so the lock is not stale at head.
The `!uv.lock` negation sits after `*.lock` in .gitignore, so it actually re-includes the lock file instead of losing to rule order.
The ruff ignore list names each UP rule and why it is off, which keeps pyupgrade from rewriting Union/Optional and typing-module hints against the 3.11 house style.
`[tool.uv] package = false` skips a build backend the script repo does not need, and the tests/__init__.py rootdir import path still holds with the new pyproject.toml at the root.

minor.name: jsonschema and referencing declared but never imported
minor.summary: pyproject.toml:6-10 lists jsonschema and referencing as runtime dependencies, but no tracked Python file (conversion/, tests/, dev2prod_DEP.py) imports either; the only third-party import is pydantic in conversion/project_model.py:6. The deps were carried over from the Pipfile, so a fresh uv sync installs two packages (and their transitive deps) the code does not use.
fix: Drop jsonschema and referencing from [project].dependencies and re-run uv lock, if nothing outside the tracked tree needs them
Keep them and note in the PR summary which planned code (for example schema validation of project_definitions/*.json) will use them

minor.name: Lock pins packages published the same day it was generated
minor.summary: uv.lock resolves pydantic 2.14.3 and pydantic-core 2.50.4 (uploaded 2026-11-05T09:15-09:17Z) and ruff 0.17.4 (uploaded 2026-11-05T18:52Z), all hours old when locked, and pyproject.toml sets no `exclude-newer` cooldown under [tool.uv]. A release that turns out broken or compromised gets frozen in by the first lock, and every future `uv lock --upgrade` keeps grabbing whatever shipped that morning. Bleeding edge, now with hashes.
fix: Add `exclude-newer = "7 days"` (relative duration, on uv versions that accept it) under [tool.uv] in pyproject.toml, then rerun `uv lock` so the pinned versions fall back to releases at least a week old.
Add an absolute RFC 3339 cutoff such as `exclude-newer = "2026-10-29T00:00:00Z"` under [tool.uv], rerun `uv lock`, and move the date forward deliberately on each upgrade.

bubble_up.reason: Supply-chain cooldown policy (none, relative 7 days, or absolute cutoff) is a developer convention call with no repo precedent, and the fix needs a uv lock the developer runs.
